title: json: optimize JSON output performance (~5x speedup)
description:
Add internal 8KB write buffer to json_dumper, eliminating thousands of individual fputc()/fputs() calls per packet. This is the dominant optimization, reducing character-by-character stdio overhead.

Additional optimizations:

- Batch indentation writes using pre-built static buffer
- Scan-ahead in json_puts_string for unescaped character runs
- Format integers via vsnprintf into internal buffer (avoid flush+vfprintf)
- Add json_dumper_value_int/uint API for printf-free integer output
- Use stack buffer for hex string conversion (avoid g_malloc/g_free per field)
- Cache first data source tvb pointer for fast-path field lookup

Measured with `-T json -x --no-duplicate-keys` on 1000-packet NGAP capture:

* Before: 31.0s
* After: 6.1s (\~5x faster)

Output is byte-for-byte identical.

AI-Assisted: yes (Kiro)

You mean like this

PERF PROFILE: ngap_1000p.pcapng (1000 NGAP packets, 2.3 GB JSON output)

 Reference: 31.0s | Optimized: 6.1s | Speedup: 5.0x

=== REFERENCE BUILD (31.0s) ===

```
49.85%  _IO_fputs                    ← character-by-character stdio
 9.10%  _IO_file_xsputn
 4.26%  jd_puts
 3.04%  __strlen_evex
 2.75%  __memmove_evex_unaligned_erms
 2.48%  get_data_source_tvb
 2.46%  __vfprintf_internal
 1.89%  fputc
 1.86%  print_newline_indent
 1.41%  jd_putc
 1.28%  write_json_proto_node_hex_dump
 1.19%  json_puts_string
```

=== OPTIMIZED BUILD (6.1s) ===

```
12.22%  get_data_source_tvb
 4.92%  write_json_proto_node_hex_dump
 4.42%  __vfprintf_internal
 4.33%  json_write_field_hex_value
 4.04%  malloc
 3.78%  _int_free
 3.58%  json_puts_string
 3.54%  proto_node_group_children_by_json_key
 2.45%  ws_label_strcpy
 2.35%  jd_putc
 2.34%  _int_malloc
 2.33%  __memmove_evex_unaligned_erms
 2.28%  _IO_default_xsputn
 2.19%  g_str_hash
 2.17%  jd_buf_append
 1.89%  proto_tree_children_foreach
 1.70%  get_data_source_tvb@plt
 1.53%  __strlen_evex
 1.39%  proto_tree_add_node
 1.21%  __strchrnul_evex
 1.20%  cfree
 1.10%  write_json_proto_node_list
 1.04%  malloc_consolidate
```

The key takeaway: \_IO_fputs went from 49.85% to gone — it was the dominant bottleneck. The profile is now flat and distributed across actual work (hex conversion, tree traversal, memory management).
